reviews.title: Disingenuous
reviews.text: So I gave Loosid a try and all was going well for a while. One day I couldn’t log in. I contacted the developers about the issue and they had noted that my account was banned for using a cartoon for my profile picture. Did it not occur to them that many of the users on this app may not want to use a personal photo? People want to stay anonymous when discussing the matters that this app was designed for. Good golly! It gets worse. I wrote a review on the play store and the developer response was just a lie. He or she indicated that I was just banned from the dating section only. Thankfully I got reinstated but now I just don’t want to taint my phone with this app because I see how disingenuous the staff is. One star is more than generous for this giant L.

reviews.title: Profiting from Recovery
reviews.text:
I’ve used this for a few months and gave it a chance. It’s clear they just want to make money off recovering addicts. For one, I constantly get notifications to buy stuff in the shop. Often, those notifications appear in other areas, like matches on the dating section. I also got a free trial that would be $30/month after I forget about it. 

You can get more from recovery groups on regular social apps. This has no groups, pages, communities, walls, events, etc. Nothing but a singular feed curated by the staff. Also, since the dating app is so limited and lacking, the community side is 50% guys commenting on women, and 50% guys trying to sound dramatic like Bill W.

It’s a proof of concept - minimally viable. Not worth $30/mo simply because it has a generic LLM attached.

reviews.title: $29 a month? For what?
reviews.text:
First of all, I reached out to the owner years ago and told him all of the things I’m about to tell you.

Big guys too busy charging people $30 a month for a terrible app.

How is it that there’s a social media that you can’t pick your username?

What year is it? 

You can get literally everything in this app other places and the $30 price tag is such a joke.

The dating app is even worse And I find that hard to believe but it’s true.

The sad truth is these people are not in the recovery business. They are in the capitalism business, and if they truly cared about people, they would make the app better and make it more affordable.

Make sure you leave them a review ! Especially if you hate the app as much as I do

reviews.title: Bummer.
reviews.text: It’s a great concept but it just doesn’t have legs. It’s like Meetup if you take away usefulness and global/local community access. There are some real folks on here eager to connect and find safe spaces to inhabit, and it’s wonderful when they find each other, but there are very nearly ZERO events anywhere in the country (they claim 1000’s), the restaurant list is populated entirely with “neighborhood bar and grill” type establishments, and most of the homepage is covered with stock photo profiles and bots giving real sober people attaboys! Even with all of the recent sober culture, there still isn’t a single worthy social platform. Loosid is an imitation of a cheesy wellness app much like The Phoenix app and it is desolate. I clicked through without signing up. Lots of full screen ads for premium features that enhance nothing.

reviews.title: It’s a GREAT concept! But the app doesn’t work very well, and seems filled with fake people
reviews.text:
Examples: I can’t change my main photo because it gives an error every time I try. I also can’t delete a photo.
Sometimes it says unable to load profile while looking through them. if you have a credit for a super like, it reminds you of this EVERY single person you see! take it easy. I haven’t found a person to “super like” yet, because almost none of the profiles have anything written in terms of text, just a lot of shiny pictures, which seem like they could easily be from a magazine. (perhaps there could be some prompts to get users to talk about what their personality is actually like? because for non-fashion models, this actually matters more ) there are some profiles that should be reported for obvious violations, but there isn’t a button to report them. it is a really excellent concept! And one that is needed in the world so hopefully they will continue developing this app. Somehow “Loosid” doesn’t sound like something a sober person would say, just a thought.

It’s like the most miserable people filtered into this one app and they are ready for blood. Be cautious.
